newsitem.title: USA: Simpson case jury starts deliberations.
newsitem.headline: Simpson case jury starts deliberations.

text.p: The O.J. Simpson civil case was turned over on Tuesday to the jury to decide if the ex-football star was responsible for the wrongful deaths of his ex-wife and her friend.

Judge Hiroshi Fujisaki told the predominantly white, seven-woman, five-man jury to disregard Simpson's acquittal in a 1995 criminal murder trial and a recent family court ruling giving Simpson custody of the two young children he had with his murdered ex-wife.
Simpson has consistently denied murdering his former wife, Nicole Brown Simpson, and her friend Ronald Goldman in June 1994. He is being sued for wrongful death by the victims' families.
If found responsible for the deaths, he could be forced to pay millions of dollars in damages.
However, according to published reports, much of Simpson's wealth has been placed in pension and trust funds which cannot be touched by the plaintiffs if they prevail in their lawsuit.

Unlike the criminal case, the civil trial jury can reach a verdict based on a "preponderance of the evidence" rather than the more rigid "beyond a reasonable doubt" and needs only a 9-3 majority to reach a decision.

The jury got the case after hearing one final emotional appeal from plaintiffs' attorney Daniel Petrocelli, who said the low point of the trial came on Monday when Simpson's attorney Robert Baker "mocked" the victims' families when he told the jury the case was about money and that it only cost $200 to file a lawsuit in California.

Brandishing $200 in bills Petrocelli strode across the courtroom to Simpson and shouted: "You know, Mr Simpson, here's $200. You want it? Give my client back his son and we will march out of here in a heartbeat." Petrocelli represents Goldman's father, Fred.
